sections.title: Summary: All Classification Metrics at a Glance
sections.body:
| Metric | Formula | Our Example | Best For |
|--------|---------|-------------|----------|
| **Accuracy** | (TP+TN)/(All) | 80% | Balanced datasets |
| **Precision** | TP/(TP+FP) | 66.7% | When FP is costly |
| **Recall** | TP/(TP+FN) | 66.7% | When FN is costly |
| **Specificity** | TN/(TN+FP) | 85.7% | Medical tests |
| **F1-Score** | Harmonic mean | 66.7% | Balance P & R |
| **AUC-ROC** | Area under curve | - | Overall ranking |
| **Log Loss** | -log(probability) | - | Probability calibration |
| **Kappa** | Chance-corrected | 0.524 | Imbalanced data |

### 🎯 Ultimate Decision Guide

sections.title: Import Required Libraries
sections.body:
Now let's implement everything we learned using Python!

```python
# Import all necessary libraries
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Sklearn metrics
from sklearn.metrics import (
    # Regression Metrics
    mean_absolute_error,
    mean_squared_error,
    r2_score,
    mean_absolute_percentage_error,
    
    # Classification Metrics
    accuracy_score,
    precision_score,
    recall_score,
    f1_score,
    fbeta_score,
    confusion_matrix,
    classification_report,
    roc_curve,
    roc_auc_score,
    log_loss,
    cohen_kappa_score,
    ConfusionMatrixDisplay
)

# Set plotting style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
sns.set_palette("husl")

print("✅ All libraries imported successfully!")
```

### Creating Sample Dataset for Regression

```python
# Creating the same example we used in theory
# House Price Prediction Example

actual_prices = np.array([50, 60, 70, 80, 100])  # Actual prices in Lakhs
predicted_prices = np.array([48, 65, 68, 85, 90])  # Predicted prices

# Create a nice dataframe to visualize
regression_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'House': [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
    'Actual Price (₹ Lakhs)': actual_prices,
    'Predicted Price (₹ Lakhs)': predicted_prices,
    'Error': predicted_prices - actual_prices,
    'Absolute Error': np.abs(predicted_prices - actual_prices),
    'Squared Error': (predicted_prices - actual_prices) ** 2
})

print("📊 House Price Prediction Dataset")
print("=" * 70)
display(regression_df)
```

### 1️⃣ Calculating MAE (Mean Absolute Error)

```python
# Method 1: Manual Calculation
absolute_errors = np.abs(actual_prices - predicted_prices)
mae_manual = np.mean(absolute_errors)

# Method 2: Using sklearn
mae_sklearn = mean_absolute_error(actual_prices, predicted_prices)

print("=" * 60)
print("📏 MEAN ABSOLUTE ERROR (MAE)")
print("=" * 60)
print(f"\nStep-by-step calculation:")
print(f"  Absolute Errors: {absolute_errors}")
print(f"  Sum of Absolute Errors: {np.sum(absolute_errors)}")
print(f"  Number of samples: {len(actual_prices)}")
print(f"\n  MAE = {np.sum(absolute_errors)} / {len(actual_prices)} = {mae_manual:.2f}")
print(f"\n✅ MAE (Manual): {mae_manual:.2f} Lakhs")
print(f"✅ MAE (sklearn): {mae_sklearn:.2f} Lakhs")
print(f"\n📝 Interpretation: On average, predictions are off by ₹{mae_manual:.2f} Lakhs")
```

**Output**

```text
============================================================
📏 MEAN ABSOLUTE ERROR (MAE)
============================================================

Step-by-step calculation:
  Absolute Errors: [ 2  5  2  5 10]
  Sum of Absolute Errors: 24
  Number of samples: 5

  MAE = 24 / 5 = 4.80

✅ MAE (Manual): 4.80 Lakhs
✅ MAE (sklearn): 4.80 Lakhs

📝 Interpretation: On average, predictions are off by ₹4.80 Lakhs
```

### 2️⃣ Calculating MSE (Mean Squared Error)

```python
# Method 1: Manual Calculation
squared_errors = (actual_prices - predicted_prices) ** 2
mse_manual = np.mean(squared_errors)

# Method 2: Using sklearn
mse_sklearn = mean_squared_error(actual_prices, predicted_prices)

print("=" * 60)
print("📐 MEAN SQUARED ERROR (MSE)")
print("=" * 60)
print(f"\nStep-by-step calculation:")
print(f"  Squared Errors: {squared_errors}")
print(f"  Sum of Squared Errors: {np.sum(squared_errors)}")
print(f"  Number of samples: {len(actual_prices)}")
print(f"\n  MSE = {np.sum(squared_errors)} / {len(actual_prices)} = {mse_manual:.2f}")
print(f"\n✅ MSE (Manual): {mse_manual:.2f} Lakhs²")
print(f"✅ MSE (sklearn): {mse_sklearn:.2f} Lakhs²")
print(f"\n⚠️ Note: Unit is Lakhs² (squared), which is hard to interpret!")
```

**Output**

```text
============================================================
📐 MEAN SQUARED ERROR (MSE)
============================================================

Step-by-step calculation:
  Squared Errors: [  4  25   4  25 100]
  Sum of Squared Errors: 158
  Number of samples: 5

  MSE = 158 / 5 = 31.60

✅ MSE (Manual): 31.60 Lakhs²
✅ MSE (sklearn): 31.60 Lakhs²

⚠️ Note: Unit is Lakhs² (squared), which is hard to interpret!
```

### 3️⃣ Calculating RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error)

```python
# Method 1: Manual Calculation
rmse_manual = np.sqrt(mse_manual)

# Method 2: Using sklearn (squared=False gives RMSE directly)
rmse_sklearn = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(actual_prices, predicted_prices))

print("=" * 60)
print("📊 ROOT MEAN SQUARED ERROR (RMSE)")
print("=" * 60)
print(f"\nRMSE = √MSE = √{mse_manual:.2f} = {rmse_manual:.2f}")
print(f"\n✅ RMSE (Manual): {rmse_manual:.2f} Lakhs")
print(f"✅ RMSE (sklearn): {rmse_sklearn:.2f} Lakhs")
print(f"\n📝 Interpretation: Predictions are typically off by ₹{rmse_manual:.2f} Lakhs")
print(f"\n💡 Note: RMSE ({rmse_manual:.2f}) > MAE ({mae_manual:.2f}) because RMSE penalizes large errors more!")
```

**Output**

```text
============================================================
📊 ROOT MEAN SQUARED ERROR (RMSE)
============================================================

RMSE = √MSE = √31.60 = 5.62

✅ RMSE (Manual): 5.62 Lakhs
✅ RMSE (sklearn): 5.62 Lakhs

📝 Interpretation: Predictions are typically off by ₹5.62 Lakhs

💡 Note: RMSE (5.62) > MAE (4.80) because RMSE penalizes large errors more!
```

### 4️⃣ Calculating R² (R-Squared)

```python
# Method 1: Manual Calculation
mean_actual = np.mean(actual_prices)
ss_tot = np.sum((actual_prices - mean_actual) ** 2)  # Total Sum of Squares
ss_res = np.sum((actual_prices - predicted_prices) ** 2)  # Residual Sum of Squares
r2_manual = 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)

# Method 2: Using sklearn
r2_sklearn = r2_score(actual_prices, predicted_prices)

print("=" * 60)
print("📈 R-SQUARED (R²) - COEFFICIENT OF DETERMINATION")
print("=" * 60)
print(f"\nStep-by-step calculation:")
print(f"  Mean of Actual Values: {mean_actual:.2f}")
print(f"  SS_total (variance from mean): {ss_tot:.2f}")
print(f"  SS_residual (variance from predictions): {ss_res:.2f}")
print(f"\n  R² = 1 - (SS_res / SS_tot)")
print(f"     = 1 - ({ss_res:.2f} / {ss_tot:.2f})")
print(f"     = 1 - {ss_res/ss_tot:.4f}")
print(f"     = {r2_manual:.4f}")
print(f"\n✅ R² (Manual): {r2_manual:.4f} = {r2_manual*100:.2f}%")
print(f"✅ R² (sklearn): {r2_sklearn:.4f} = {r2_sklearn*100:.2f}%")
print(f"\n📝 Interpretation: Model explains {r2_manual*100:.2f}% of variance in house prices!")
```

**Output**

```text
============================================================
📈 R-SQUARED (R²) - COEFFICIENT OF DETERMINATION
============================================================

Step-by-step calculation:
  Mean of Actual Values: 72.00
  SS_total (variance from mean): 1480.00
  SS_residual (variance from predictions): 158.00

  R² = 1 - (SS_res / SS_tot)
     = 1 - (158.00 / 1480.00)
     = 1 - 0.1068
     = 0.8932

✅ R² (Manual): 0.8932 = 89.32%
✅ R² (sklearn): 0.8932 = 89.32%

📝 Interpretation: Model explains 89.32% of variance in house prices!
```

### 5️⃣ Calculating Adjusted R²

```python
# Adjusted R² = 1 - (1 - R²) * (n - 1) / (n - p - 1)
# where n = number of samples, p = number of features

n = len(actual_prices)  # 5 samples
p = 2  # Assuming 2 features (e.g., area and bedrooms)

adjusted_r2 = 1 - (1 - r2_manual) * (n - 1) / (n - p - 1)

print("=" * 60)
print("📊 ADJUSTED R-SQUARED")
print("=" * 60)
print(f"\nFormula: Adj R² = 1 - (1 - R²) × (n - 1) / (n - p - 1)")
print(f"\nGiven:")
print(f"  R² = {r2_manual:.4f}")
print(f"  n (samples) = {n}")
print(f"  p (features) = {p}")
print(f"\nCalculation:")
print(f"  Adj R² = 1 - (1 - {r2_manual:.4f}) × ({n} - 1) / ({n} - {p} - 1)")
print(f"         = 1 - {1 - r2_manual:.4f} × {n-1} / {n-p-1}")
print(f"         = 1 - {(1 - r2_manual) * (n-1) / (n-p-1):.4f}")
print(f"         = {adjusted_r2:.4f}")
print(f"\n✅ Adjusted R²: {adjusted_r2:.4f} = {adjusted_r2*100:.2f}%")
print(f"\n💡 Note: Adjusted R² ({adjusted_r2*100:.2f}%) < R² ({r2_manual*100:.2f}%) due to penalty for features")
```

**Output**

```text
============================================================
📊 ADJUSTED R-SQUARED
============================================================

Formula: Adj R² = 1 - (1 - R²) × (n - 1) / (n - p - 1)

Given:
  R² = 0.8932
  n (samples) = 5
  p (features) = 2

Calculation:
  Adj R² = 1 - (1 - 0.8932) × (5 - 1) / (5 - 2 - 1)
         = 1 - 0.1068 × 4 / 2
         = 1 - 0.2135
         = 0.7865

✅ Adjusted R²: 0.7865 = 78.65%

💡 Note: Adjusted R² (78.65%) < R² (89.32%) due to penalty for features
```

### 6️⃣ Calculating MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error)

```python
# Method 1: Manual Calculation
percentage_errors = np.abs((actual_prices - predicted_prices) / actual_prices) * 100
mape_manual = np.mean(percentage_errors)

# Method 2: Using sklearn (returns as a ratio, so multiply by 100)
mape_sklearn = mean_absolute_percentage_error(actual_prices, predicted_prices) * 100

print("=" * 60)
print("📊 MEAN ABSOLUTE PERCENTAGE ERROR (MAPE)")
print("=" * 60)
print(f"\nStep-by-step calculation:")
for i, (actual, pred) in enumerate(zip(actual_prices, predicted_prices)):
    pct_error = abs(actual - pred) / actual * 100
    print(f"  House {i+1}: |{actual} - {pred}| / {actual} × 100 = {pct_error:.2f}%")
print(f"\n  Sum of percentage errors: {np.sum(percentage_errors):.2f}%")
print(f"  MAPE = {np.sum(percentage_errors):.2f}% / {len(actual_prices)} = {mape_manual:.2f}%")
print(f"\n✅ MAPE (Manual): {mape_manual:.2f}%")
print(f"✅ MAPE (sklearn): {mape_sklearn:.2f}%")
print(f"\n📝 Interpretation: On average, predictions are off by {mape_manual:.2f}%")
```

**Output**

```text
============================================================
📊 MEAN ABSOLUTE PERCENTAGE ERROR (MAPE)
============================================================

Step-by-step calculation:
  House 1: |50 - 48| / 50 × 100 = 4.00%
  House 2: |60 - 65| / 60 × 100 = 8.33%
  House 3: |70 - 68| / 70 × 100 = 2.86%
  House 4: |80 - 85| / 80 × 100 = 6.25%
  House 5: |100 - 90| / 100 × 100 = 10.00%

  Sum of percentage errors: 31.44%
  MAPE = 31.44% / 5 = 6.29%

✅ MAPE (Manual): 6.29%
✅ MAPE (sklearn): 6.29%

📝 Interpretation: On average, predictions are off by 6.29%
```

# Create a comprehensive summary visualization

axes[0, 0].set_title('📏 Error Metrics Comparison', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Value', fontsize=12)
for i, (name, val) in enumerate(zip(metrics_names, metrics_values)):
    axes[0, 0].text(i, val + 1, f'{val:.2f}', ha='center', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Plot 2: R² visualization (pie chart style)
r2_pct = r2_manual * 100

axes[0, 1].pie(sizes, explode=explode, labels=labels, colors=colors_pie,

║  MSE  (Mean Squared Error)      :  {mse_manual:.2f} Lakhs²           ║
║  RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error) :  {rmse_manual:.2f} Lakhs            ║
║  R²   (R-Squared)               :  {r2_manual:.2%}               ║
║  Adj R² (Adjusted R²)           :  {adjusted_r2:.2%}               ║
║  MAPE (Mean Absolute % Error)   :  {mape_manual:.2f}%                ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
"""
axes[1, 1].text(0.5, 0.5, summary_text, transform=axes[1, 1].transAxes, 
                fontsize=12, verticalalignment='center', horizontalalignment='center',
                fontfamily='monospace', bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='lightblue', alpha=0.8))
